headline: Doctor and hospital lobbyists, a health insurer and the AI company Anthropic are helping write guidelines that state medical boards could use to regulate AI in medicine.
score_reason: Specific and relevant, but early-stage and confidential; no rules adopted yet.
importance_line: It could shape which AI tools may act on patients with little doctor oversight, affecting patients and doctors first, state medical boards next and AI and insurance companies, though the guidelines are only a draft not yet public.
summary: STAT reports that a 22-member workgroup convened by the Federation of State Medical Boards, which includes the American Medical Association, the American Hospital Association, Anthropic and the insurer Elevance Health, met in private in Washington in early October to draft guidelines on AI in medical practice. FSMB chief Humayun Chaudhry told STAT a draft could appear in weeks to months and might later underpin state laws, with particular attention to AI tools that act with little or no direct physician supervision.
notes: Only the free intro of a STAT+ article was available (about 2,200 characters), so detail beyond that is not covered.
